It locks the selected qualifying run, not every historical run before filtering. There is already an indexable PR restriction: /tmp/frozen-75215/products/stamphog/backend/models.py:142 declares a normal Django ForeignKey for pull_request (indexed by default), also present in migrations/0001_initial.py:274-282, and the migration declares team_id db_index=True at :220. votes.refutation: I first looked for an existing index and followed the entire queryset to its evaluation. The foreign-key index can narrow by PR, and first() evaluates the combined filtered query; Python method order does not make PostgreSQL lock all PR history before WHERE filtering. The remaining claim depends on unusually large per-PR history and an unprovided execution plan or timing. No caller loop or demonstrated workload in the cited change establishes that cost, while ordinary unrelated task saves are excluded. This is a possible future query optimization built on a contradicted locking premise, not a verified defect.

votes.evidence: products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1202-1209 builds one SQL queryset constrained by team, pull_request and head_sha, excludes terminal failure/superseded statuses, orders by created_at, and selects first(). select_for_update() is a query modifier; its position in the method chain does not execute locking before subsequent filters. The resulting bounded filtered query does not lock every historical PR run as claimed. ReviewRun.pull_request is a normal indexed Django ForeignKey (models.py:142; migrations/0001_initial.py:274-280), and team_id is also indexed (the same migration:220), so this is not an unindexed scan of all reviews. The candidate history is that single PR's history.
votes.refutation: I checked the existing indexes, query construction, and deduplication behavior. There is no matching composite index, but absence alone does not establish the claimed scanning/locking defect. PostgreSQL applies the WHERE predicates before locking qualifying rows; first() also limits the selected result. Same-head saves do not grow review history, as tested in test_tasks.py:974-1020, and state-only saves do not trigger this query (products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:85-89). A composite index could be a useful measured optimization for unusually large PR histories, but no query plan, workload, or reachable harmful history size establishes a shipping slowdown. The broad-lock premise is false and the remaining performance claim is speculative.

votes.refutation: I first checked the claimed scan-and-lock mechanism and existing indexes. The missing composite index is real, but the claimed locking behavior is contradicted by the filtered, limited SELECT FOR UPDATE query: nonmatching historical heads are not all locked simply because the ORM method appears earlier in the chain. A composite index might improve unusually large per-PR histories, but no production cardinality, query plan, latency, or contention evidence establishes a material regression beyond the already-indexed per-PR lookup. This is a speculative indexing optimization built partly on an incorrect locking premise, not a demonstrated shipping defect.
